instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the ANSYS graphical user interface (Workbench, Mechanical, MAPDL GUI, or Fluent GUI as applicable). Do not open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, MAPDL batch input files, PyMAPDL, PyFluent, journal files run from shell, Python, or any helper script/code that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Use only ANSYS native GUI tools, menus, dialogs, and built-in solve/save commands. Use the ANSYS Workbench GUI to complete a linear eigenvalue buckling analysis. Physical problem: A pin-ended straight column is subjected to axial compression. Coordinate system and geometry: - Use the global Cartesian coordinate system. - Model the column as a line body with a beam cross-section. - The column axis is along the global Y direction. - The bottom end is located at Y = 0 mm. - The top end is located at Y = 1000 mm. - The rectangular beam section is: - Width = 10 mm - Height = 10 mm Model parameters: - Line body length: 1000 mm - Section type: rectangular beam section - Section size: 10 mm × 10 mm - Material: Structural Steel with the following linear elastic properties: - Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa - Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3 - Use a consistent N-mm unit system. Boundary conditions: - Bottom end at Y = 0 mm: - Constrain UX = 0, UY = 0, and UZ = 0. - Leave all rotations free. - Top end at Y = 1000 mm: - Constrain UX = 0 and UZ = 0. - Leave UY free. - Leave all rotations free. - Apply an axial compressive reference load of 1 N at the top end in the negative global Y direction. Analysis type: - Linear eigenvalue buckling analysis. - Extract the first buckling mode. Save requirements: - Use C:\Users\user\Desktop as the working location. - Save the Workbench project file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\wb_buckling.wbpj - Save the MAPDL-equivalent database file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\wb_buckling.db - Save the MAPDL-equivalent structural result file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\wb_buckling.rst Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated. You must complete all operations interactively through the graphical user interface (GUI) step by step. The use of external script files is strictly prohibited.
